assessments.support: Raw N (1112) and post-QC N (1111: 573 controls, 538 ASD) by diagnosis are reported, with training/test split sizes given.
A custom SPM8-based preprocessing pipeline with HOG voxel-based features is described, but no atlas/parcellation is used since features are image-texture based rather than ROI connectivity.
ASD/control labels taken from ABIDE; diagnostic-instrument source not independently restated beyond a reference citation.

Feature selection (MRMR) and hyperparameter tuning were performed via 5-fold cross-validation strictly on the training set, with final evaluation on a completely held-out test set never used during model/feature selection — an explicit leakage-avoidance design. However, site was used directly as an input feature rather than harmonised or held out, which could allow the classifier to partly exploit site identity rather than disorder-related signal.

risk_of_bias.summary: Methodologically careful train/hold-out split with feature selection and tuning confined to the training set (avoiding peeking), but site is included as a raw predictive feature rather than harmonised, and no connectivity atlas/parcellation or explicit motion-metric threshold is reported.

charting.title: Using Functional or Structural Magnetic Resonance Images and Personal Characteristic Data to Identify ADHD and Autism
charting.primary_goal: Build a single automated learning pipeline (MHPC) to classify ADHD (ADHD-200) and autism (ABIDE) from functional/structural MRI and personal characteristic data
charting.country_region: Multi-site (17 institutions, North America and Europe)
charting.data_types: resting-state fMRI, structural MRI, personal characteristic data (age, sex, handedness, IQ measures, site, eye status)
charting.dataset_openly_available: Yes — ABIDE and ADHD-200 datasets are both publicly available online; no separate analysis code repository mentioned
charting.feature_types: Voxel-based image texture (3D Histogram of Oriented Gradients) + personal characteristic data
charting.specific_features: 3D-HOG features extracted from functional or structural MRI (no ROI/atlas parcellation); feature selection via minimum-redundancy-maximum-relevance (MRMR)
charting.feature_extraction_tools: SPM8 + in-house MATLAB preprocessing pipeline (motion correction, co-registration, spatial normalization to MNI)
charting.importance_method: MRMR feature selection; features mapped back to brain regions
charting.model_category: Ensemble of classical ML base learners (MHPC system)
charting.specific_algorithms: Linear SVM, RBF-kernel SVM, decision trees, k-nearest neighbours, naive Bayes
charting.validation_methodology: 5-fold cross-validation on the training set for feature selection (MRMR) and hyperparameter tuning; final single evaluation on a held-out test set (889 train / 222 test, label-balanced random split)
charting.key_performance_results: ABIDE hold-out: Functional MRI 59.2% (baseline 51.6%), Structural MRI 60.1%, Personal Characteristic 59.6%, Structural+PCD 64.1%, Functional+PCD 65.0% (best) accuracy.
charting.summary_key_findings: Combining resting-state fMRI-derived HOG features with personal characteristic data achieved the best ABIDE hold-out accuracy of 65.0% (baseline 51.6%), outperforming functional MRI alone (59.2%), structural MRI alone (60.1%), and PCD alone (59.6%), and outperforming the then-best published ABIDE result (60.0% over a 53.6% baseline).
charting.reviewer_notes: Site of imaging is used as an input feature rather than harmonised away or held out, which may let the classifier partly learn site identity rather than purely disorder-related signal.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (MHPC ensemble); ABIDE, N=1111 (573 controls, 538 ASD) from 17 institutions, split into 889 training / 222 hold-out test subjects.
narrative_row.methods: SPM8-based preprocessing; 3D-HOG voxel-texture features from functional and/or structural MRI combined with personal characteristic data; MRMR feature selection and classifier/hyperparameter tuning via training-set cross-validation; single evaluation on a held-out test set.
narrative_row.outcomes: Best ABIDE accuracy 65.0% (functional MRI + personal characteristics) vs 51.6% baseline, exceeding functional MRI alone (59.2%), structural MRI alone (60.1%) and PCD alone (59.6%).
narrative_row.key_limitations: No connectivity atlas/parcellation used; site of imaging used as a raw feature rather than harmonised; no specific motion-metric threshold reported.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: A clear example of hold-out-set discipline (feature selection/tuning strictly on training data) for ABIDE predictive modelling, though site handling via raw feature inclusion is methodologically distinct from harmonisation or leave-site-out approaches used elsewhere in this corpus.

kg_link.cohort_description: 1111 individuals (573 controls, 538 ASD) from 17 institutions, after excluding 1 of 1112 subjects for a preprocessing failure; randomly split into an 889-subject training set and a 222-subject hold-out test set.
kg_link.finding: Combining resting-state fMRI (3D-HOG features) with personal characteristic data achieves 65.0% hold-out accuracy on ABIDE (baseline 51.6%), the best of five feature combinations tested and an improvement over the prior best published ABIDE result.
